hook: An internal email chain between 12 AF/DET 3 and the Office of the Undersecretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security confirms that two brief UAP sighting reports from April 10–11, 2025 in the INDOPACOM AOR are cleared for release at the UNCLASSIFIED level.
why_it_matters: This document reveals the bureaucratic mechanism by which raw UAP observation data is reviewed and downgraded for public or inter-agency release, showing that even minimal sighting reports (duration, no interference) require sign-off from the Undersecretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security before unclassified dissemination. The two tearlines confirm active UAP reporting by aircrews operating in the INDOPACOM theater as recently as April 2025. The classification framework visible here—SECRET//NOFORN wrapper around UNCLASSIFIED core data—illustrates how operational UAP data is compartmented even when the underlying observation contains no classified details.

key_findings.finding: A US aircraft observed a possible UAP for 12 seconds on April 10, 2025 at 2353Z in the INDOPACOM AOR, with unknown altitude, unknown speed, and no interference noted.

quotes.text: US AIRCRAFT OBSERVED 1X POSS UAP FOR 12 SECONDS AT 2353Z, FLYING AT UNK ALTITUDE AND UNK SPEED, NO INTERFERENCE WAS NOTED.

key_findings.finding: A second UAP observation occurred the following day, April 11, 2025 at 0007Z, lasting 23 seconds, also with unknown altitude, unknown speed, and no interference.

quotes.text: US AIRCRAFT OBSERVED 1X POSS UAP FOR 23 SECONDS AT 0007Z, FLYING AT UNK ALTITUDE AND UNK SPEED, NO INTERFERENCE WAS NOTED.

key_findings.finding: An Information Disclosure Analyst from the Office of the Undersecretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security is the approving authority confirming these tearlines are cleared at the UNCLASSIFIED level.

quotes.text: I wanted to clarify that these tearlines are approved at the UNCLASSIFIED level.

key_findings.finding: A PAROC Intel Data Analysis Technician at 12 AF/DET 3 verified with the flying unit that both the observation lines and the INDOPACOM AOR designation are unclassified, indicating a multi-step classification review process for UAP reports.

quotes.text: I just got oﬀ the phone with the unit that ﬂies
that the two lines listed are on the UNCLASSIFIED level and that adding in the AOR as INDOPACOM is also at the UNCLASSIFIED level.

key_findings.finding: The overall email chain is classified SECRET//NOFORN despite the UAP sighting data itself being approved at UNCLASSIFIED—demonstrating that the classification wrapper protects the identities of personnel and the unit involved, not the observation content.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: The document reflects the current UAP reporting and disclosure pipeline within DoD, consistent with AARO's mandate to standardize and disseminate UAP incident data.

The Office of the Undersecretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security involvement in approving UAP data release reflects the broader intelligence community oversight structure that historically includes cross-agency coordination.
